fields.sample_size: survey population: 130 members (mostly one per household) of a coffee marketing and multiservice cooperative in San Jose and a census list of 115 households in the second community (sex-disaggregated survey, 2016); plus interviews, participant observation and community water-quality testing 2014-2019; number of completed surveys not extracted
fields.effect_estimate: Households in both Nicaraguan communities average 2 months of drinking-water insecurity in the dry season followed by 2.5 months of food insecurity early in the growing season; durations of lean food months are similar across communities and sexes, but water insecurity lasted longer in the community with weaker local institutions and less surface water. Ethnography documents gendered experiences (e.g. 8 women vs 18 men reported owning milpa plots), conflicts over irrigation versus domestic uses, and cross-scalar institutional limits (water committees, CAPS) during the 2014-2017 drought. Comparative case study; the institutional contrast is two communities, not a tested effect.
fields.study_design: mixed-methods comparative case study of two communities (sex-disaggregated survey, interviews, participant observation, water-quality testing, drought analysis)
fields.section: Full text: Methods (survey, ethnography, water testing); Results (food and water lean months by community and sex); Discussion; Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Methods (survey, ethnography, water testing); Results (food and water lean months by community and sex); Discussion; Conclusions

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a mixed-methods comparative case study of two neighbouring Nicaraguan smallholder communities (survey of about 130 co-op members and a 115-household census list plus 2014-2019 fieldwork), read in full text 2026-10-04. Water insecurity (about 2 months) lasted longer where local institutions were weaker; gender and conflict shape access. Two-community comparison.

notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds the survey population and the gendered ownership detail. 'Weaker institutions' is a descriptive contrast between two communities, not an estimated effect. MMAT rating left in place.
